HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PAINTED INTRO-CARD. INTIMATE THREE-SHOT of the hill sisters, faces LARGE in the central band. LOW from the water. ONE DEVICE: the mirror waterline as a cyan-and-ember painted stroke. FOREGROUND: Golhwa orange #e86820 CENTER, legs open on wet rock, hiked chima, wanting face (#7 sheet). Hyullé cyan #2eb8c4 RIGHT, knees pressed, shy wrecked face (#8). Narim green #3d9e52 LEFT, breathless (#6). White jeogori, character-color chima, matching binyeo. Magical cavern steam: ember motes, water-luminescence, floating leaf-light — the CAVE is coloured, not a body halo. FAR ledge small: Dangun apex, Hyukgose and Alyoung REDRAWN as painted webtoon (SECOND, THIRD), Suro purple far left (LEFT), Heo deep-brown skin purple silk far right (FOURTH). Munmu a speck in the mouth. Jewel colour, visible brush, paper grain. Match sister faces to the sheet. One of each. No sitting class photo. No text. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = suro, SECOND face = hyukgose, THIRD face = alyoung, FOURTH face = heohwangok, FIFTH face = dangun, SIXTH face = narim, #7 face = golhwa, #8 face = hyulle, #9 face = munmu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board alyoung (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), binyeo board heo (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. KING SURO — Look: His portrait face: young, warm, a thin moustache and goatee, black hair under a little gold crown. Dress: Purple silk robe with gold-ochre collar bands and sash, as on his portrait. Crown: Gaya gold crown: a gold band with tall upright grass-leaf finials and hanging jade gogok. Now: As a ghost in the steam cavern (647) he keeps his portrait's young face, purple silk and little gold crown — never an old white-bearded hermit; barefoot, feet in the water, delighted with himself. Colour #e0a33c. HYUKGOSÉ — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #6f9fe8. QUEEN HU — Look: South Indian princess from Ayuta: deep warm brown skin, clearly darker than every Gaya and Samhan face around her; large dark kohl-lined eyes, full lips, straight nose, blue-black hair coiled low with the purple-tiger binyeo, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Her portrait silk: violet-purple jeogori with magenta-gold patterned sleeves and cream cuffs, deep violet chima, pale gold sash with tassels. Cut close and tailored: the jacket fitted to the bust and waist, the sash cinched high, the skirt falling clean from the hips; elegant and expensive, never loose, never a sari dump, never pink. Crown: Gaya gold crown: a gold band with tall upright grass-leaf finials and hanging jade gogok. Colour #d98fa8. DANGUN Colour #b8956a. NARIM Colour #3d9e52. GOLHWA Colour #e86820. HYULLÉ Colour #2eb8c4. KING MUNMU — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #C41E3A. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
